paper.title: Responsible Task Automation: Empowering Large Language Models as Responsible Task Automators
paper.central_claim: ResponsibleTA enhances responsible task automation through pre-execution feasibility, post-execution completeness and local-memory privacy protection, comparing prompted generic models against domain-specific learned assistants.

evidence.quote: we detail its related prompt design as illustrated in Figure 5
evidence.support_explanation: Text locates the Figure5 completeness prompt. It was absent from the serialized text and subsequently read in the fixed image supplement; FIG5 records that inspection, rather than inferring the prompt from prose.
Diagram confirms pre-action feasibility, post-action completeness and local placeholder-to-value resolution before executor.

Full prompt read: Windows feasibility role; command plus current UI elements with ID, Content and Location. BBC finance example returns Thought and Feasible: No; no matching element. User-query template and response schema visible.
Visual encoder plus language decoder predicts typed feasibility token; login on unrelated blog returns 0.
Amazon example rejects nonexistent sort-by-price element; replaces with Sort by: Featured; completion check rejects partial progress until Price: Low to High selected.

Full prompt read: Windows completeness role; executed command plus current UI elements with ID, Type and Content. Sports-news example treats presence of sports-related headlines as completion; this can confuse content relevance with successful navigation. Thought plus Completeness Yes/No schema; no before-state comparison.
Full first trajectory page read including low-level Edge/input/search/sort commands and corrective Step6 Price: Low to High.

Full second trajectory page read: cheapest charger selection uses minimum y after sort; See All Buying Options opens panel, then additional Add to Cart action needed. Displayed page supports interface correction, not globally cheapest-item verification.
CPython ZIP failure: planner repeats Download ZIP while Codespaces tab shown; guard rejects; human reference requires Local then Download ZIP. Correct rejection does not guarantee recovery.

signatures.information: Current screenshot+command before execution; resulting screenshot+command after execution. Screen-parser element descriptions shown to coordinator only on replanning. DOM/UIA used to make training labels, not inferred as deployment privilege.
signatures.operation: Binary trained or prompted feasibility verdict -> gate/replan; execute; binary completeness verdict -> continue/replan. Stop at preset retry count (value not supplied in prose).
signatures.conditions: Visible verifiable progress and sufficiently capable coordinator; retry cap; accurate parser/judges.
signatures.feedback: Generated screenshot-command training labels plus runtime learned verdicts; these are not sound executable oracles.
signatures.selection_rule: Domain-specific paradigm chosen by5K common test subset; execution allowed on feasible verdict.
signatures.selection_data: Feasibility1M/100K pairs from~40K pages; completeness1.2M/60K from113K/6K pages. Split by source site not established.
signatures.persistence: Trained auxiliary weights fixed; per-task replanning context only, no retained learned improvement across tasks.
signatures.later_use: Same fixed architecture on12 real-world cases.
signatures.claimed_effect: 3->8->10 successful tasks/12; offline classifier accuracy gain.
signatures.failure_boundary: Single-screenshot visual incompleteness, synthetic negatives, false verdicts, and coordinator deadlocks.

signatures.information: NER receives raw instruction locally; cloud receives placeholders; local executor receives resolved values. Replanning can upload screen descriptions.
signatures.operation: Replace literal -> store local key/value -> cloud plan placeholder -> resolve locally.
signatures.conditions: Sensitive spans detected/marked; no leak through screen descriptions, generated text or malicious content.
signatures.feedback: Two benign utility checks; no attack-success or leakage-recall measurements.
signatures.selection_rule: NER extraction or user-defined placeholders; no empirical redaction threshold given.
signatures.selection_data: No privacy test corpus; two case comparisons.
signatures.persistence: Local sensitive-value dictionary (not a reusable experience/skill memory).
signatures.later_use: Resolve placeholders during current task; no retained performance-improvement claim.
signatures.claimed_effect: Avoid sending selected private literals; no utility loss in2 cases.
signatures.failure_boundary: NER misses/context leakage, malicious requesting of values, sensitive UI text on replan; no formal security guarantee.

gap.author_gap: Summary API descriptions do not encode executor feasibility or completion; cloud coordinators risk private literal disclosure.
gap.checked_gap: Own related-work §2.2 acknowledges SayCan executable affordances and DEPS/Plan-Eliminate-Track feedback. Exact novelty is integration of pre/post guards plus local substitution, not discovery of feedback planning. Primary antecedent papers absent in fixed bundle.

lineage.source: Pix2Seq and Donut-style document understanding per §3.2, Appendix C.1

gap.residue: Pre/post reliability handoff in screen-only UI execution and local sensitive literal handling.
gap.stakes: Wrong but plausible commands can fail or harm; high-level plan/executor mismatch.
gap.method_response: Two separately trained screen-command binary guards plus local placeholder dictionary.
gap.remaining_gap: General responsibility and privacy not proved by synthetic classifier metrics and12 benign tasks.
unresolved: Primary ancestor fulltexts not fixed; lineage constrained to assigned paper account.

claims.text: ResponsibleTA enhances responsible task automation through pre-execution feasibility, post-execution completeness and local-memory privacy protection, comparing prompted generic models against domain-specific learned assistants.
claims.setting: Swin+BART learned auxiliaries, GPT4 coordinator, own visual executor;12 live web/Windows cases
claims.baseline/control: Same coordinator/executor; no guards vs+feasibility vs+completeness. Security module in all; two benign placeholder comparisons.
claims.selection_vs_test: Learned classifier heldout splits; exact on-policy case selection/development disjointness not reported.
counterevidence: Tiny selected case suite without repeat
No threat model, leak-recall or adaptive attack audit
Completion prompt demonstration conflates relevant content with achieved command goal.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Available text supports a promising demonstration of visual guards and literal substitution, not general secure/responsible automation.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Authors report3/12 ->8/12 ->10/12 successful live cases and improved heldout synthetic guard metrics; literal substitution preserves utility in2 benign cases. This supports small-scale guard integration, not general responsibility or privacy assurance. No worker reproduction.
unresolved: No natural on-policy judge audit, attack-based leakage test, independent online repetitions or matched-retry baseline.
